findings.issue: The 'equal in all three: data order' case passes even if the `a.index - b.index` term were removed from compareLeaks, because candidates are generated by walking LEAK_CATEGORIES and Array.prototype.sort is stable, so ties keep data order anyway.
findings.evidence: src/stats/leaks.ts sessionLeaks builds candidates via LEAK_CATEGORIES.flatMap(...) before .sort(compareLeaks); the output is correct either way, so this is not a behaviour gap, only a test that can't tell the explicit tie-break apart from sort stability.
findings.fix: None required. Leave as is: the explicit index term keeps the comparator a total order on its own. Optionally note in the test comment that data order is also guaranteed by construction.

summary: The comparator is a lexicographic order over (major desc, exact integer rate desc, errors desc, unique data index asc). Because the last key is a unique index, it is a strict total order: antisymmetric, transitive, and it never returns 0 for distinct candidates. The rate term `y.errors*x.decisions - x.errors*y.decisions` is negative exactly when x's rate is higher, which matches the spec. Products of per-session counts stay far below 2^53, so the integer comparison is exact. Sorting runs on a fresh candidates array built from LEAK_CATEGORIES and the slice to MAX_SHOWN_LEAKS comes after the sort, so the input is never mutated (the test checks this against a structuredClone). The tests would catch a wrong ranking. AC#1 fails if rate is put before Major (B is 80% vs 60%) or if hinted Majors are counted (7 > 5). AC#3 fails if the cap is applied before the sort (data order would keep flop-fold and flop-call). AC#2 and the 5/8 > 4/8 > 9/20 unit case fail if the rate direction is flipped. The unit errors tie-break is checked in both input orders. The cap is checked at 5/4/3/2/0 leaks, and unknown categories ('preflop-raise') and non-leaks are ignored. The targeted suites pass locally, and gate fix-2 passes on test, lint, typecheck, scope and test integrity. Scope matches the spec's 5 files. ReportScreen has only a doc-comment change and there is no new user-visible text. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
